units.title: Introduction and Approaches to Social Research
units.topics: Meaning and significance of social research, The relationship between theory and research, Approaches in social research: positivist, critical, interpretative, feminist, Ethics of social research.

units.title: The Research Process
units.topics: Steps in social research, Hypothesis: meaning, characteristics and types, Research design: meaning and types, Types of social research: basic and applied research.

units.title: Sources of Data
units.topics: Sources of data: primary and secondary data, Primary data sources: fieldwork, surveys, interviews, Secondary data sources: census, government reports, institutional records, libraries, digital databases, Advantages and limitations of secondary sources.

units.title: Sampling Techniques
units.topics: Meaning and importance of sampling in social research, Key concepts: population, sample, sampling frame, Types of sampling: probability sampling (simple random, stratified, systematic, cluster) and non-probability sampling (convenience, purposive, quota, snowball).

units.title: Research Foundations and Approaches
units.topics: Application of research approaches, Ethical issues in research, Formulation of hypothesis, Identification of research design, Pure and applied research exercises, Theory and research link analysis.

units.title: Data Sources and Sampling Plan
units.topics: Identification of data sources, Selection of population and sample, Applying sampling techniques, Preparation of sampling plan, Group presentation and viva.

units.title: Forces Shaping Contemporary India
units.topics: Colonialism: Impacts on economy, society, law, Modernization: Western education, urbanization, Globalization: Post-1991, integration, cultural flows, Nation-building: Gandhi (swaraj, villages), Nehru (secular modernism) and Ambedkar (caste annihilation, rights).

units.title: Political and Democratic Contours
units.topics: Indian Democracy: Successes and challenges, Democratic values and institutions: Preamble, fundamental rights, Parliament, Election Commission, Secularism and communalism, Justice, equality and freedom in contemporary India.

units.title: Agrarian Transformations
units.topics: Agrarian structure: Land relations, caste-class nexus, Commercialization, green revolution and its socio-ecological impacts, Agrarian distress, farmers' indebtedness, Contemporary farmers' movements and rural employment issues.

units.title: Emerging Realities
units.topics: Digital Society: Digital divide, surveillance, online culture, Environmental movements and climate justice, Social media, public sphere, and political mobilization, New forms of inequalities: caste, gender, class in the knowledge economy.

units.title: Understanding Youth Culture
units.topics: Youth culture: concept and approach (fashion, music, slang, digital culture, social norms), Social institutions shaping youth culture (family, education, caste, class, gender), Subculture and counterculture among youth, Youth and generational conflict (Millennial, Gen Z and Alpha).

units.title: Contemporary Youth Culture and Social Issues
units.topics: Youth in the digital age: social media influence, online identity, FOMO, Youth and consumer culture: lifestyle, leisure, brand consciousness, Contemporary youth challenges: unemployment, educational pressure, addiction, emotional issues, Youth activism and participation in social change.

units.title: Introduction to Urban Sociology
units.topics: Meaning, nature, and scope of Urban Sociology, Development of Urban Sociology: Chicago School, Rural-urban continuum and urbanism as a way of life (Louis Wirth), Urbanization: concept, trends, and patterns.

units.title: Urban Spaces and Urban Challenges in India
units.topics: Urbanization in India: historical context and post-independence trends, Spatial segregation: gated communities, slums, and squatter settlements, Urban infrastructure and civic challenges: housing, water, waste, transport, Sustainable cities and urban governance.

units.title: Understanding Crime and Deviance
units.topics: Concept and definitions of crime, deviance, and delinquency, Sociological theories of crime: Anomie theory (Durkheim, Merton), Differential Association theory (Sutherland), Labelling theory (Becker), Types of crime: violent crime, property crime, white-collar crime, organized crime, cybercrime.

units.title: Criminal Justice System and Contemporary Issues
units.topics: Structure of Criminal Justice System in India: Police, Judiciary, Correctional administration, Prison system in India: overcrowded prisons, rights of prisoners, prison reforms, Emerging issues: gender-based violence, hate crimes, juvenile delinquency.

units.title: Concepts and Perspectives on Agrarian Society
units.topics: Agrarian sociology: meaning, scope, and significance, Agrarian social structure: landownership, caste and class hierarchy, Agrarian classes in India: landlords, rich peasants, middle peasants, small/marginal farmers, landless agricultural labourers.

units.title: Agrarian Transformation and Contemporary Issues
units.topics: Land reforms in India: objectives, achievements, and failures, Green Revolution and agrarian capitalism, Commercialization, contract farming, and agrarian distress, Farmers' suicides, rural livelihood diversification, and contemporary agrarian movements.

units.title: Research Methods
units.topics: Quantitative and qualitative research: meaning, nature, and differences, Survey method: meaning, nature, advantages, and limitations, Case study method: meaning, nature, advantages, and limitations.

units.title: Techniques of Data Collection
units.topics: Observation: techniques, types (participant, non-participant), advantages, and limitations, Interview: techniques, types (structured, unstructured), advantages, and limitations, Questionnaire: construction, types, advantages, and limitations.

units.title: Data Processing and Analysis
units.topics: Data processing: editing, coding, classification, and tabulation, Quantitative data analysis: measures of central tendency, percentages, graphical representation, Qualitative data analysis: thematic analysis, content analysis.

units.title: Research Report Writing
units.topics: Meaning, significance, and structure of a research report, Steps in report writing, Citation styles (APA, MLA) and referencing, Plagiarism and academic integrity in social research.

units.title: Data Collection Techniques
units.topics: Designing observation schedule, conducting participant/non-participant observation, drafting structured questionnaire, designing interview schedule.

units.title: Fieldwork and Data Analysis
units.topics: Conducting pilot study and fieldwork, data coding and tabulation, basic statistical calculations, preparing short research report and presentation.

units.title: Urban Transformations and Challenges
units.topics: Urbanization in India: uneven development and inequalities, Civic issues: water scarcity, transport congestion, waste/pollution management, Slums and housing: growth, governance (PMAY), social implications.

units.title: Media, Democracy and Public Sphere
units.topics: Role of media in Indian democracy: freedom, accountability, elections, Commercialization, sensationalism, and fake news, Social media, digital public sphere, and echo chambers, Post-truth era and mediatization of politics.

units.title: Education and Health Systems in India
units.topics: Education in India: access, equity, privatization, New Education Policy (NEP 2020), Health system in India: public vs. private healthcare, affordability, health inequalities.

units.title: Contemporary Social Movements and Ecological Challenges
units.topics: Contemporary social movements: Dalit, tribal, women's, and ecological movements, Climate change, environmental crises, and climate refugees, Demographic challenges: ageing, migration, and urbanization.

subjects.title: Introduction to Human Rights and Social Justice

units.title: Basic Concepts in Human Rights and Social Justice
units.topics: Human Rights: Definition, meaning, and characteristics, Social Justice: Meaning and principles (equity, liberty, dignity, participation, diversity), Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR).

units.title: Human Rights and Social Justice in Indian Context
units.topics: Constitutional provisions: Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles, and human rights, Social justice and vulnerable groups: SCs, STs, OBCs, women, children, minorities, persons with disabilities, Role of National/State Human Rights Commissions and Judiciary.

subjects.title: Introduction to Human Rights and Social Justice (Practical)

units.title: Human Rights Awareness Campaign
units.topics: Poster presentation and awareness activities on human rights violations, rights of children, gender equality.

units.title: Social Justice Institutional Visit
units.topics: Visit and observe public institutions, schools, courts, or NGO initiatives working for human rights and social justice, preparing observational report.

units.title: Introduction to Sustainable Development
units.topics: Meaning, definition, and characteristics of sustainable development, Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): Overview and targets, Role of governance, NGOs, and civil society in promoting sustainability.

units.title: Dimensions of Sustainability
units.topics: Social dimension: Equity, social justice, indigenous knowledge, Economic dimension: Green economy, sustainable agriculture, circular economy, Environmental dimension: Climate change, pollution, biodiversity conservation, sustainable resource management.

units.title: Crime, Deviance and Community Study
units.topics: Field-based observation of community crime perceptions, cybercrime awareness survey, police station visit and interaction.

units.title: Social Control, Rehabilitation and Crime Prevention
units.topics: Study of correctional institutions, NGOs working with prisoners and juvenile homes, rehabilitation strategies and report preparation.

units.title: Emergence of Sociological Thought – Intellectual and Social Context
units.topics: a) The Enlightenment and its influence on sociological thinking b) The French Revolution and the transformation of social structures c) Impact of the Industrial Revolution and Urbanization

units.title: The Positivist School
units.topics: a) Auguste Comte: Positivism and the Law of Three Stages b) Concepts of Social Statics and Social Dynamics c) Emile Durkheim: Division of Labour and Social Integration, Theory of Suicide

units.title: Karl Marx
units.topics: a) Theory of Class and Class Conflict b) Concept of Alienation in Capitalist Societies c) Theory of Surplus Value and Exploitation

units.title: Max Weber
units.topics: a) Types of Authority and the Structure of Bureaucracy b) The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism c) Social Action: Concept and Typology

units.title: Exploring Social Change: Then and Now
units.topics: a) Imagine you are a sociologist in 18th century. Write a short paragraph: What Social Issues and problems would you want to study in society back then? b) Visit or observe a busy area in your town and write what you see about jobs, housing, or traffic—link it to industrialization and urbanization.

units.title: Understanding Social Issues
units.topics: a) Take a problem (like poverty or crime) and compare: Common-sense view vs Sociological view. b) Look at a social problem (like unemployment or school dropouts). Apply positivist approach: What data/facts could you collect to study it? Apply an interpretive approach: What questions would you ask people to understand their feelings and experiences?

units.title: Social Reality: Class Conflict and Collective Values
units.topics: a) Interview people from different socioeconomic backgrounds: One daily wage earner, one middle-class professional, and one business owner. Discuss: How does income affect their life chances, work culture, and future aspirations? b) Identify a social custom or ritual in your community. Explain how it promotes unity and social cohesion, reflecting Durkheim's idea of the collective conscience.

units.title: Society and Everyday Life: Gender Roles and Social Influence
units.topics: a) Contact different age/gender people and find out how their families, peers, and mass media have influenced their choices, beliefs, or behavior. b) Track your own daily schedule and categorize tasks into instrumental actions and value-driven actions.

units.title: Introduction
units.topics: a) Meaning and definition of health and public health b) Social Dimension of health c) Social issues of health in India- Poverty, unemployment, Ignorance, Blind faith, Backwardness, Urbanization, Stress, Lack of facilities, Pollution, Malnutrition d) Health services in India- From charity to rights

units.title: Social Policy and Action on Health
units.topics: a) Health Issues and the diversities b) National Health Mission and Ayushman Bharat Yojana c) Role of civil Society in health care system d) Career opportunities in public health

units.title: Social Issues
units.topics: a) Definition, Characteristics, Causes and Consequences b) Searching for alternatives to the issues-State and its policies, Civil society and action, whistleblowing.

units.title: Issues related with Women, Youth and Environment
units.topics: Issues related with Women: a) Domestic violence: causes, forms, and impact b) Sexual harassment: Meaning, Types (Verbal, Non- Verbal and Physical), c) Dowry-related abuse: inequality, exploitation, and violence. Issues related with Youth: a) Socio-Economic Challenges, Educational Inequality, and unequal opportunities Lack of opportunities, Depression, stress and anxiety among youth. b) Employment Issues – growing unemployment, casualization, challenges of globalization, digitalization and AI c) Suicide and substance abuse- depression, stress and anxiety, social media addiction. Issues related with Environment: a) Meaning of Environment and Ecological Degradation b) Major Environmental Issues: Climate change, deforestations, Water Scarcity and Pollution c) Environmental Movements in India: Chipko, Narmada Bachao Andolan, Save Silent Valley, Western Ghats Bachao Abhiyan

units.title: Understanding Social Challenges through Direct Engagement
units.topics: a) Visit and report on an NGO working on mental health, women's empowerment, youth issues, or the environment. b) Interview with a local community leader or activist regarding prevailing social problems.

units.title: Youth, Substance Abuse, and Mental Well-being
units.topics: a) Gender violence laws: Effectiveness and gaps. b) Reservation and affirmative action: Current relevance and future scope. c) Digitalization and employment: Opportunities vs. job insecurity. d) Role of youth in climate justice: Responsibility vs. inaction.

units.title: Environment, Community Action, and Sustainability
units.topics: a) Reservation policy and caste inequality. b) Impact of social media on youth mental health. c) Climate change and its disproportionate impact on marginalized communities. d) Gender wage gap and economic inequality.

units.title: Synthesis and Advocacy
units.topics: a) Prepare an awareness poster on social issues. b) Group presentation on findings from NGO visit or community interview.

units.title: Introduction to Social Media
units.topics: a) Definition and Meaning of Social Media b) Types of Social Media c) Significance of Social Media in Contemporary Society d) Uses and Gratification Theory

units.title: Contemporary Challenges of Social Media
units.topics: a) Addiction of Social Media b) Social Media: Mental Health and Social Isolation c) Fake News and Disinformation d) Surveillance, Privacy, and Cyber Bullying

units.title: Introduction to the Indian Constitution
units.topics: Preamble-Source and Objects a) Sovereign and Republic b) Socialist and Secular c) Democratic

units.title: Fundamental Rights and Duties
units.topics: a) Values reflected in fundamental rights b) Values reflected in fundamental duties c) Values reflected in directive principles of state policies

units.title: Emergence of Sociology in India
units.topics: a) The Colonial Background b) Nationalism c) Development of Sociology in India (Pre-Independence and Post-Independence period)

units.title: Indological Perspective
units.topics: a) G.S. Ghurye - Indology and Theory of Caste b) Irawati Karve - Kinship in India c) Louis Dumont – Pure and Impure

units.title: The Structural Functional Perspective
units.topics: a) M. N. Srinivas - Dominant Caste and Sanskritization b) S. C. Dube - Indian Village c) A. M. Shah – Family in India

units.title: The Marxist Perspective and the Subaltern Perspective
units.topics: a) A. R. Desai – Concept of Class, Social Background of Indian Nationalism b) D. D. Kosambi - Historical Materialism c) B. R. Ambedkar - Annihilation of Caste, Origin of Untouchability d) Sharad Patil – Non-Brahminical Perspective

units.title: Historical Context
units.topics: a) Timeline Preparation of your own family and kinship ties. b) Essay Writing on a key thinker's contribution to the evolution of the discipline.

units.title: Indological Perspectives
units.topics: a) Kinship Mapping b) Create a kinship chart based on Irawati Karve's classification c) Write a reflective note on how kinship structures influence marriage, inheritance, and social support systems in your own community.

units.title: Structural Functional Perspective
units.topics: a) Field Visit to a Village or Semi-Urban Area गाव/वाडा/वस्ती/टोला/पाडा/वाहतुक नगर b) Observation of village social structure: settlement patterns, caste dynamics, community spaces (panchayat, temple, chaura/chavadi). c) Conduct short interviews on the role of the dominant caste, changing village leadership, and self-governance. d) Write a field report on social harmony and conflict in the selected area.

units.title: Marxist Perspectives
units.topics: a) Field visit to a factory or workshop or office or agricultural setting (focus on labour relations, working conditions, and wage disparities). b) Conduct a small survey on occupational mobility across two generations.

units.title: Subaltern Perspectives
units.topics: a) Critical reading and group discussion on extracts from Dr. B. R. Ambedkar's Annihilation of Caste or Sharad Patil's writings. b) Prepare a creative presentation on how marginalization is experienced in everyday life.

units.title: Reflective and Comparative Analysis
units.topics: a) Seminar on Indian Sociology Today: Synthesis of Different Perspectives. b) Group debate: Which sociological perspective is most relevant for understanding contemporary Indian society?

units.title: Introduction
units.topics: a) Concept of Ageing b) Issues of Aged: Social, Economic, Physical, Psychological, Medical, Gender c) Role of Elderly people in India d) Causes and consequences of Ageing

units.title: Care and Concern of Old Aged
units.topics: a) Care and welfare need of Aged and Senior Citizens: physical needs, healthcare needs, retirement, singleness, adjustment, violence, neglect, abuse. b) Role of Family, State, and NGO's for wellbeing for Aged. c) Policies for Aged

units.title: Social Stratification
units.topics: a. Meaning, definition Consequence and characteristics of social stratification b. Bases of stratification: Caste, class, gender c. Social Exclusion: Meaning and definitions d. Types of social exclusion

units.title: Social Mobility
units.topics: a. Meaning and definitions b. Types of social mobility (horizontal, vertical, intergenerational intragenerational) c. Opportunities for social mobility, Obstacles in upward social mobility d. Critical issues: Caste, Class, gender, Race, Ethnicity, Disability and Social Mobility in India.

units.title: Stratification and Mobility: Contemporary trends
units.topics: a) Socio-economic transformation and changing trends of social mobility (Impact of changing patterns of occupation, industrialization, urbanization, Technology) b) Observe correlation between economic and social mobility (Case studies) c) Role of Welfare State model to promote upward mobility. (impact of welfare policies on social mobility) d) Impact of Education on social mobility (Is the educational system a mechanism of inter-generational transmission of advantages and disadvantages or not?) e) Consequences of stratification: lifestyles and consumption patterns, educational attainment

units.title: Stratification and Exclusion
units.topics: a) Caste, Class, Gender and Exclusion: Observe the correlation between 1. Use of public space, 2. Access to basic resources, 3. Education and health outcomes, 4. Identity and dignity. b) Disability and Exclusion: Invisible Barriers. c) Spatial Exclusion (Residential segregation in Indian cities: slums, gated communities, caste based localities/neighborhoods).

units.title: Understanding Social Harmony
units.topics: a) Understanding Concept of harmony (freedom from aggression) with field visit and observation; examples of social harmony- celebrating diverse cultural festivals, fostering understanding, respect, and unity among different communities, tolerance, mutual respect, cooperation, secularism and peace, egalitarianism and social justice. (Concepts only) b) Understanding link between Indian philosophical and cultural tradition of harmony (ganga - jamani tehjeeb) c) Post-Independence period: Constitutional core of harmony -towards humane and multicultural India d) Globalized world: Coexistence and harmony (issues of environment and risks, wars, north-south divide, and cultural clashes)

units.title: Achieving Social Harmony through Social Inclusion
units.topics: a) Concept and characteristics of social inclusion and social exclusion; Social Inclusion as a means to harmony b) Understanding dimensions of Inclusion (developing sense of belonging, sharing; getting options, choice and control, seeking voice, chance and participation) Majoritarianism, power of the few, inequality, as hurdles in social inclusion. Conduct case studies, field visit, observations, film review, group seminar. c) Promoting Social Inclusion and Harmony; Respect for diversity, empathy and compassion, dialogue and communication, conflict resolution, education and awareness, volunteerism and community engagement, state and institutional support, inclusive and sustainable development and livelihood. Conduct case studies, field visit, observations, film review, group seminar.

units.title: Beginning of the Reading and Writing
units.topics: a. Reading as form of data, critique and reflections b. Types of Writing: stories, biography, autobiography, popular writing, academic writing c. Read a short (1-2 page) academic text of moderate difficulty and Summarize it in one paragraph (5-6 sentences). d. Re-read the same text and re -write the summary again after a brief discussion of its form (is the summary well structured, clear and effective? The architecture of arguments: main, subsidiary, minor. Everything is not equally important)

units.title: Techniques for Reading and Writing Texts
units.topics: a) लिंगभाव समजून घेताना – कमला भसीन (श्रुती तांबे) or Kamla Bhasin 'What is Gender': Students should read the book together, note down important points from it, note the similarities and differences between the book and the surrounding reality, and write a essay on how a boy and a girl are socially constructed in their own family. b) उपरा, बलुतं, कोल्हटयाचं पोर, आयदान, आक्कलमाशी (of these Upara and Baluta are translated into English. English medium students can use them) - The students should read any two of these autobiographies together, note the important points in it, observe how the author has explained and discuss.
